item.title: hook and cron CLI, doctor hooks section, composition, user docs

results.statement: atm hook register must read an integer TIMEOUT_MS constant from the module's text, store it on the registration, and refuse a module that lacks one.
results.quote: 7. the timeout should probably be a required field of the hook python module i.e. const int timeout_ms = 1000.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test registers a module file without TIMEOUT_MS and asserts a typed refusal; with TIMEOUT_MS = 1000 the row's timeout_ms is 1000
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: atm doctor, run for a team with an active hook registration, must invoke the module's doctor() through the hook runner and report the reply in a hooks section of the doctor report.
results.quote: the plug-in can run this check as part of 'doctor' it provides and IF a hook is installed, 'atm doctor' would call hook.doctor() when called from the team it is registered for.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:15Z (Rand, round 3: no sha header)
results.deterministic_check: a test with an active registration for team T whose doctor() returns {"success": true, "message": "ok"} asserts run_doctor for T has a hooks section containing that reply
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: atm computes, stores and compares no sha of a hook module; module drift is detected only inside the module's own doctor() reply.
results.quote: I may have made a mistake. when atm-bd is published, the sha must be calculated and stored in a manifest for every file. then the installer can check against the published manifest to verify the file has not changed. we should do this for the entire skill. all agents/skills/python files.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:15Z (Rand, round 3: no sha header); withdraws the round-2 sha header. Session 2026-10-18, Rand: 'yes, drift detection becomes 100% atm-db responsibility and is done through hook.doctor'
results.deterministic_check: rg -n 'sc_sha|sha256|released_sha' on the hook, cron and doctor sources matches nothing; hook_registration has no sha column
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: A cron schedule names a hook module and its args; on each tick atm must invoke that module's cron entry with those args under the same request and reply contract as task hooks.
results.quote: b) we can register a cron function in the same python module the hook resides. cron would be registered on 'phase start' and shut-down on 'phase complete' and the method for atm-bd would simply call 'atm-bd cron <args>'.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: a test with module M and args ["--phase", "bk"] asserts the tick's HookRequest has hook cron.tick and request.args equal to those args, and that the module's argv is exactly [module_path, "cron.tick"] with the args only in the stdin request
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: The atm CLI must have the subcommands cron start, cron end and cron list: start creates an active schedule, end marks one or every schedule of a phase inactive, list prints them.
results.quote: we would have 'atm cron start', 'atm cron end', 'atm cron list'.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: atm cron --help lists start, end and list; a CLI test runs each against the in-process router
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: Every cron schedule must be created with exactly one stop condition, a time (--until) or a stop hook (--until-hook); atm cron start must refuse a schedule with none or both, and the stored row must carry the condition.
results.quote: there should probably be a 'stop condition' which was mandetory when it is created which would generally be a time, but a function/hook would also be useful.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 6257077671 (Rand, round 4, 2026-10-18), relayed on PR #1877
results.deterministic_check: a CLI test runs atm cron start without a stop flag and with both flags and asserts a usage error and no request; the cron_schedule CHECK rejects a row with neither until_at nor stop_hook and one with both
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: A schedule started with --until-hook must have the daemon call the module's stop entry (hook name cron.stop, same stdin shape) before each scheduled run; a reply of stop true with a reason must end the schedule with that reason recorded and run nothing, stop false must run the tick, and a malformed reply must skip the tick and leave the schedule active.
results.quote: a function/hook would also be useful. for atm-bd cron, phase bead closing would be condition for stopping.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 6257077671 (Rand, round 4, 2026-10-18), relayed on PR #1877
results.deterministic_check: a paused-clock test with DummyHookRunner stop replies {stop:true,reason:r}, {stop:false} and a malformed reply asserts respectively: row ended with last_outcome stopped: r and no cron.tick call; one cron.stop then one cron.tick call; row still active and no cron.tick call
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: Hooks run inside the daemon process through one HookRunner shared by the task router and the cron worker; the atm CLI never spawns a hook process.
results.quote: Hooks run inside the daemon process through one HookRunner shared by the task router and the cron worker; the atm CLI never spawns a hook process.
results.context: phase-bk design decision docs/plans/phase-bk/design.md §3 D-3 (fenix, PR #1877); not a Rand ruling
results.deterministic_check: rg -n 'process::Command' crates/atm/src matches no hook code; HookRunner is constructed once in atm-daemon-bootstrap and handed to the router and the cron worker
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: The atm CLI must have the subcommands hook register <hook> --module <path> --phase <x> [--cwd <dir>], hook disable --phase <x> [<hook>] and hook list [--phase <x>] [--json].
results.quote: The atm CLI has the subcommands hook register <hook> --module <path> --phase <x> [--cwd <dir>], hook disable --phase <x> [<hook>] and hook list [--phase <x>] [--json].
results.context: phase-bk design decision docs/plans/phase-bk/design.md §6 (fenix, PR #1877); not a Rand ruling
results.deterministic_check: atm hook --help lists register, disable and list with those flags; a CLI test runs each against the in-process router
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: Hook and cron behavior is tested with a fixture hook module and a paused tokio clock; no test starts, targets or depends on a live daemon.
results.quote: Hook and cron behavior is tested with a fixture hook module and a paused tokio clock; no test starts, targets or depends on a live daemon.
results.context: phase-bk design decision docs/plans/phase-bk/design.md §7 (fenix, PR #1877); not a Rand ruling
results.deterministic_check: rg -n 'atm daemon|ATM_DAEMON|spawn.*daemon' on the new tests matches nothing; cron tests use #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: An active hook replaces the atm task subcommand call: atm runs the hook first, parses its JSON reply, and the subcommand's own logic runs only when the reply is pass-through.
results.quote: so the hooks replace the call. the hooks should return json which is processed by atm. We should be able to replace quite a few of (perhaps all) atm task subcommands.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test registers a task.assign hook whose reply is success false and asserts the task ledger is unchanged and the command fails with the hook's message

exclusion.reason: replacing the subcommand call with the hook and acting on its reply is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds the registry and cron commands and the doctor section

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: replacing the subcommand call with the hook and acting on its reply is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds the registry and cron commands and the doctor section.

results.statement: A hook registration is keyed by (team, phase, hook); disabling a phase marks every hook of that team and phase inactive instead of deleting the rows.
results.quote: 1. the skill would register the hooks as 'active' for a phase for a single team, when phase ended, hooks would be disabled.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: hook_registration has UNIQUE(team, phase, hook) and an active column; a test disables a phase and asserts the rows remain with active = 0 and disabled_at set

exclusion.reason: disable keeps the row in bk-1's store; bk-5's atm hook disable only sends the HookDisable envelope and prints the rows

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: disable keeps the row in bk-1's store; bk-5's atm hook disable only sends the HookDisable envelope and prints the rows.

results.statement: atm passes every hook one JSON request of a single published schema carrying the full subcommand request plus the caller's identity, team and host; the top-level shape is the same for every hooked command.
results.quote: 2. atm would call the hook w/ all info passed in + info of caller (who ran the hook) in a single json schema which is known and same for every command for that hook.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: one test serializes HookRequest for all six task hooks and cron.tick and asserts the same top-level keys: schema_version, hook, team, phase, caller, request, custom

exclusion.reason: the one request schema is bk-2's HookRequest; bk-5 sends no hook request

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the one request schema is bk-2's HookRequest; bk-5 sends no hook request.

results.statement: A success false reply must stop the subcommand before any of its logic runs, with the reply's message returned to the caller as the command error.
results.quote: if 'bd ready' false, atm-task-assign hook returns false and message to caller i.e. { success = "false" message="bead {bead-id} is not ready" }
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a hook fixture prints {"success": false, "message": "bead x is not ready"}; the test asserts no task row is written and the error carries that message

exclusion.reason: the refused path is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the refused path is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic.

results.statement: When a hook replies success true with no atm-action list, atm runs the subcommand's normal logic with the original request, giving the same result as when no hook is registered.
results.quote: or if 'bd ready' the hook either retruns { success = "true" } and atm proceeds w/ normal atm task assign logic
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test with a hook replying {"success": true} asserts the resulting task row equals the row produced with no hook registered

exclusion.reason: pass-through is bk-3's router path; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: pass-through is bk-3's router path; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic.

results.statement: A success true reply with an atm-action array must make atm run each action in array order instead of the original subcommand's logic.
results.quote: OR the hook returns what to do { success = "true" atm-action[] = { action-1, action-2 } } where action-1 and action-2 would be atm json commands. i.e. action-1 could be exactly the same command that was input, action-2 could be 'atm send omega-prime@hermes <escelation-message>'.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test with a reply carrying two actions asserts both ran in order and the original request was not applied

exclusion.reason: action dispatch is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: action dispatch is bk-3's router; bk-5 adds no task subcommand logic.

results.statement: Each atm-action entry is an atm command expressed as the same JSON body the daemon's HTTP API accepts for that command and is deserialized with that route's request type.
results.quote: 4. how I described #3 this would be true. an array of 'un-hooked' atm commands would be returned as json exactly the same as they would be passed over http.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test deserializes an atm-action entry's request field with the same serde type the HTTP route handler for that command uses

exclusion.reason: the action entry type is bk-2's HookAction; bk-5 parses no reply

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the action entry type is bk-2's HookAction; bk-5 parses no reply.

results.statement: atm never consults a hook while executing an action returned by a hook; every atm-action entry runs through the un-hooked command path.
results.quote: the hook would not be called recursively, so the { success = true } (pass-through case) would simply do the same thing 'atm task assign ...' would do if there was no hook.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test whose task.assign hook returns an atm-action task.assign asserts the hook process was spawned exactly once

exclusion.reason: hooks-disabled dispatch is bk-3's router flag; bk-5 dispatches no action

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: hooks-disabled dispatch is bk-3's router flag; bk-5 dispatches no action.

results.statement: An atm-action entry's as field is the identity the action runs as: atm dispatches the action with that caller identity, and an entry without as runs as the original caller.
results.quote: 6. yes
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal); point 6 of the proposal read: 'returned actions may run as the lead'
results.deterministic_check: a test dispatches {command: task.assign, as: team-lead} from caller cipher and asserts the task row's assigner is team-lead

exclusion.reason: the as field is bk-2's HookAction::envelope and bk-3's dispatch; bk-5 dispatches no action

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the as field is bk-2's HookAction::envelope and bk-3's dispatch; bk-5 dispatches no action.

results.statement: atm itself never performs a bead-tracker (bd) read or write; every bd call happens inside the hook process.
results.quote: 5. yes
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal); point 5 of the proposal read: 'bead writes stay inside the hook'
results.deterministic_check: rg -n '"bd"|\.beads' crates/ matches nothing new on the sprint diff

exclusion.reason: bk-5's commands send envelopes and read TIMEOUT_MS; no bd call is possible from them, and the rule's code-level check is bk-3's

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: bk-5's commands send envelopes and read TIMEOUT_MS; no bd call is possible from them, and the rule's code-level check is bk-3's.

results.statement: The hook runner uses the registration's timeout_ms as the hook call's deadline: a hook still running at the deadline is killed and the command fails with HOOK.TIMEOUT.
results.quote: This allows the hook to KNOW when it's caller will timeout so it can set a shorted timeout to complete w/out error.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal) (point 7, second sentence)
results.deterministic_check: a paused-clock test with a sleeping fixture hook and timeout_ms 100 asserts the child is killed and the error code is HOOK.TIMEOUT

exclusion.reason: deadline enforcement is bk-3's DaemonHookRunner; bk-5 spawns no hook

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: deadline enforcement is bk-3's DaemonHookRunner; bk-5 spawns no hook.

results.statement: Each of the six atm task subcommands (assign, start, close, move, list, events) must have its own hook name and consult its registered hook.
results.quote: assign,start,close are natural to override w/ hooks. we might as well hook the others
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: the hook name enum has task.assign, task.start, task.close, task.move, task.list, task.events and cron.tick; one test per subcommand asserts the hook is consulted

exclusion.reason: hooking the six subcommands is bk-3's router consult; bk-5 touches no task subcommand

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: hooking the six subcommands is bk-3's router consult; bk-5 touches no task subcommand.

results.statement: A task subcommand with no active hook for the caller's team and phase must run its existing logic unchanged and report no hook-related warning or error.
results.quote: since all hooks would be optional (defaulting to normal behavior in the case of missing), I don't see much risk.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: the existing task CLI integration tests pass with no hook_registration rows and their output is unchanged; the router's request path makes no hook_registration store call (the in-memory snapshot is the only lookup; store call counter 0 after construction)

exclusion.reason: the no-hook default is bk-3's snapshot path; bk-5 touches no task subcommand

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the no-hook default is bk-3's snapshot path; bk-5 touches no task subcommand.

results.statement: Cron schedules are persisted as cron-expression strings in a new cron_schedule table of the atm SQLite database.
results.quote: atm cron would be a simple scheduler w/ cron strings saved in a new table in atm db.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: the migration creates cron_schedule with a cron_expr TEXT column; a test inserts and reads a schedule back through CronScheduleStore

exclusion.reason: the cron_schedule table is bk-1; bk-5's atm cron start only sends the CronStart envelope

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the cron_schedule table is bk-1; bk-5's atm cron start only sends the CronStart envelope.

results.statement: Every active cron_schedule row is loaded when the daemon starts, so a schedule created before a daemon restart keeps firing after the restart with no re-registration.
results.quote: cron would be persistent after restarting daemon.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T23:04Z (Rand, round 2)
results.deterministic_check: a paused-clock test inserts an active schedule, starts CronWorker from the store, advances past the next fire time and asserts one hook invocation

exclusion.reason: restart survival is bk-1's table and bk-4's active_all load at worker start; bk-5 composes the worker but asserts composition through run_now, not a restart

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: restart survival is bk-1's table and bk-4's active_all load at worker start; bk-5 composes the worker but asserts composition through run_now, not a restart.

results.statement: A cron tick's hook reply goes through the same reply handler as a task hook's: an atm-action list is dispatched through the same un-hooked action path, and success false is recorded as the tick outcome.
results.quote: the cron design would be 'atm cron' and it would run a hook (just like the atm task hooks) at a predefined interval AND return a set of atm commands just like we described above.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal) (cron note)
results.deterministic_check: a test with a cron.tick reply carrying one send action asserts a persisted message and a last_outcome of success

exclusion.reason: cron reply actions reach the task-hook dispatcher inside bk-4's tick; bk-5 only composes AtmCron

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: cron reply actions reach the task-hook dispatcher inside bk-4's tick; bk-5 only composes AtmCron.

results.statement: The hook request's custom field carries JSON defined by the hook's owner; atm passes it through unchanged and never validates or interprets it.
results.quote: the atm-task-close hook would accept a 'custom' json set of fields which would be defined by the custom python (not atm). atm would simply pass the json to the python function
results.context: atm-bd-orchestration #340 (Rand, 2026-10-18), the origin of atm-core #1873; carried as phase-bj ANC-064 until the bj/bk split
results.deterministic_check: a test passes custom {"x": [1, {"y": null}]} and asserts the hook's stdin carries it byte-equal under the custom key

exclusion.reason: the custom field is bk-2's HookRequest; bk-5 sends no hook request

results.explanation: Excluded from this bead by the anchor's exclude list: the custom field is bk-2's HookRequest; bk-5 sends no hook request.

results.statement: A schedule started with --until <time> must end when that time is reached: the row is set inactive with ended_at and last_outcome stopped: until reached, and no run happens at or after that time.
results.quote: which would generally be a time

results.statement: The hook runner must start a hook with exactly the environment ATM_HOOK=1, ATM_TEAM, ATM_PHASE, PATH and HOME in the registered cwd, passing no other variable from the daemon's environment.
results.quote: The hook runner starts a hook with exactly the environment ATM_HOOK=1, ATM_TEAM, ATM_PHASE, PATH and HOME in the registered cwd, and passes no other variable from the daemon's environment.

results.statement: The cron worker parses each cron_expr with the cron crate in UTC and sleeps until the next occurrence computed from Utc::now() after every run, never replaying ticks missed while the daemon was stopped.
results.quote: The cron worker parses each cron_expr with the cron crate in UTC and sleeps until the next occurrence computed from Utc::now() after every run, never replaying ticks missed while the daemon was stopped.
results.context: phase-bk design decision docs/plans/phase-bk/design.md §5 D-4 (fenix, PR #1877); not a Rand ruling

results.statement: A schedule whose previous run is still in flight when its next tick is due skips that tick and logs the skip; two runs of one schedule never overlap.
